canon.text: The AI gateway is owned by the Agent Infrastructure team. Earlier sources named the AI Gateway team as the owner, but those facts are out of date and were replaced by the Agent Infrastructure team.

sentences.text: The AI gateway is owned by the Agent Infrastructure team.
sources:
Agent Infrastructure (2026-10-10): What we own
- **AI gateway**: the single endpoint PostHog's AI features use to call LLM providers, with shared auth and cost attribution
- **Tasks and sessions**: the infrastructure that runs agents in cloud sandboxes
- **AI metering**: real-time usage and spend tracking for every LLM call and agent run. We work with the [Billing team](/teams/billing) to make sure that usage gets billed
- **Agent package**: the shared agent runtime that other teams build their agents on
- **Hog harness**: our custom agent harness, built on Pi. It captures product intent and passes it to the model, which leads to better generations. It ships as the [Pi option in PostHog Desktop](/docs/posthog-desktop/use-any-model-and-harness)

AI Gateway (2026-09-23): The AI gateway is PostHog's internal routing layer for calling LLM providers. It gives PostHog's AI features a single endpoint to call, with shared handling for things like provider routing, caching, fallbacks, and cost attribution. The team owns the gateway service, its provider integrations, the [AI Observability Playground](/docs/ai-observability/playground), and the seams where the gateway connects into the rest of PostHog – particularly AI Observability team.

sources:
Sprint - September 21 to October 2 (2026-09-28): A community member, 2026-09-17:
🟡 Improve HogQL query quality and performance. Continue query analysis, guidance and guardrails. Goal-level completion measures still need confirmation.
🟡 Protect ClickHouse from disproportionate query usage. Andy has proposed event-volume-scaled API read-byte limits, initially in shadow mode. The scaling window remains open for discussion. Proposal
⚪ Monitor query regressions and develop automated investigation. Confirm the agreed first delivery and success measure during Q4 planning.
HogQL DevEx / ClickHouse support: confirm current priorities and status for experiment logs, legacy endpoints and JSON-column work; no completion is inferred from missing updates.
Ownership transition: dashboards, actions, exports, subscriptions and alerts are moving to Product Analytics. Carry remaining product work in the handover, with any finishing commitments explicitly agreed. Handover context

self-driving: let users create and edit inbox reports through the MCP (2026-09-30): self-driving: let users create and edit inbox reports through the MCP
Why
Only a scout run can author an inbox report today.
A person using their own agent over the PostHog MCP can edit parts of a report, but cannot create one, so findings from their own harness either stay outside PostHog or go through a scout they do not need.
There is no strong reason to keep report authoring scout-only: a report created by a named user through the MCP has a clear audit trail (the user and the API key), and it passes the same safety judge and validation a scout report does.
This issue specs letting users create reports through the MCP and bringing report edits to parity with

Duplicate inbox reports and competing PRs for one fix (tracking) (2026-08-27): Duplicate inbox reports and competing PRs for one fix (tracking)
Tracking issue for the class of failure where Self-driving opens several inbox reports, or several PRs, for one underlying fix. Two production cases on 2026-08-27 surfaced three distinct mechanisms; each child issue closes one of them and is labelled self-driving for implementation.
Mechanisms and issues
A. Grouping retrieval miss (same signal text, different reports)

#90184 grouping never searches with the signal's own embedding

B. Shared root cause invisible to grouping (different signals, same fix)

#90178 error-tracking signals omit the event origin (host, dev-host flag)
#90186 skip auto

feat(signals): ship events-only default pre-checks for six product scouts (2026-10-11): feat(signals): ship events-only default pre-checks for six product scouts
Problem

Six product scouts spend a full sandbox run on most projects only to find that the product is absent and write a not-in-use: entry.
Each of these close-outs reads only the events table, so a default pre-check can make the same decision before the sandbox starts.

Refs #115162

Origin

Scout: a custom scout
First signal: 2026-10-11
Inbox report: open
Task started by: auto-start, after the report was rated P2 and ready to fix

sources:
Customer support (2026-09-18): What do Support Engineers do?
Right now, support engineers provide the first level of support for most engineering teams and [specialize in certain products](/handbook/support/support-smes).

Support engineers respond to and solve as many tickets as they can for these products, or escalate tickets to the appropriate product engineering team if needed. There are certain products where the engineers on those teams are directly responsible for support:
 - Security
 - Merch
 - Wizard & Docs
 - Clickhouse and infrastructure teams
 - Any team whose product is not yet in GA

When we hire new support engineers they will usually spend the first few weeks focused just on analytics related tickets, until they've started to build more familiarity with the platform as a whole.

Overview (2026-10-05): How marketing works
Marketing at PostHog is a collaborative effort across several teams. There are seven distinct teams that handle different aspects of marketing:

- Graphics team – Leads all art, design, illustration, and brand work for PostHog
- Website team – Leads all matters related to posthog.com and handles some product design aspects
- Developer Marketing team – A multidisciplinary team that handles Product Marketing, partnerships, and other unowned marketing tasks
- Editorial team – Leads content, newsletters, and social
- Video team – Leads video
- Wizard & Docs team – Leads on documentation and the wizard
- Builder Relations team – Leads in-person events, the forum, and Discord

If you're not sure who to talk to, check [Who can help me?](/handbook/marketing/ownership).

sentences.text: The Website team appears to be responsible for PostHog.com, since its listed responsibilities include making PostHog.com the best resource for learning how to use PostHog.

- Ensure PostHog.com is the best resource for learning how to use PostHog

- Support small teams in meeting their goals by providing design and copywriting support

sentences.text: An earlier team page also listed the AI Gateway team as owner of the AI Observability Playground, and that listing was replaced by the Agent Infrastructure team ownership.
sources: AI Gateway (2026-09-23): The AI gateway is PostHog's internal routing layer for calling LLM providers. It gives PostHog's AI features a single endpoint to call, with shared handling for things like provider routing, caching, fallbacks, and cost attribution. The team owns the gateway service, its provider integrations, the [AI Observability Playground](/docs/ai-observability/playground), and the seams where the gateway connects into the rest of PostHog – particularly AI Observability team.

sentences.text: The security team, referred to as team-security, is the team that handles security findings.
sources:
Support hero (2026-09-28): Security findings
Work through the findings for your team during your rotation. If you cannot finish one, hand it over to the next support hero. If you are not sure how serious a finding is, or how to fix it, ask in `#team-security`.

chore(security): route only embargoed fixes to posthog-private (2026-10-13): chore(security): route only embargoed fixes to posthog-private
Problem

Devs and agents open PRs in PostHog/posthog-private for minor security fixes that could be public.
The routing rule sends a fix private whenever publishing it "would reveal the weakness", which covers almost any security fix.
A private fix is only worth it for an embargo, where team-security pauses the private sync, disables the merge queue, and ships through the security sync flow.

Changes

Security fixes now go to PostHog/posthog by default.
posthog-private is only for a severe vulnerability that team-security agrees needs an embargo.
"Severe" means an attacker can exploit live cod

Working in PostHog Support (2026-07-24): Security tickets
- When a new security ticket is received, [this workflow](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/workflows/019d9146-223a-0000-8165-1a3489e88b3d/workflow) auto-closes some known spam. If the ticket isn't known spam, we tag it with `team_security`, assign it to the security team, auto-respond to the customer letting them know about our disclosure program, and then notify `#security-reports`.

fix(insights): hide the trends click hint when a click cannot open people (2026-10-12): fix(insights): hide the trends click hint when a click cannot open people
Problem

A trends chart can offer "Click to view people" in its tooltip, but the click does nothing.
The bar, line and lifecycle charts show the hint when the persons modal is on. The click handler also needs a query source to build the actors query, and returns early without it.

Changes

The tooltip shows the click hint only when a click can open the persons modal or call the context callback.
canHandleTrendsChartClick holds this check next to handleTrendsChartClick. The three charts use it in place of their own copies.
Split out of #105735, which is now only the scene-load fix.
